seo.meta_title: Is TGI Fridays Closing? Bankruptcy, Owner & 2026 Status
seo.meta_description: TGI Fridays isn't going out of business, but it has shrunk to roughly 70 to 80 U.S. restaurants after its 2024 bankruptcy. Who owns it now and what's next.

question: Is TGI Fridays Closing?
quick_answer: TGI Fridays is not shutting down, but it is much smaller than it used to be. The company that ran its own restaurants filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in November 2024, and the U.S. chain has shrunk to roughly 70 to 80 restaurants in 2026, down from more than 600 at its 2008 peak. The brand is now owned by Sugarloaf Holdings, led by former CEO Ray Blanchette, which plans to grow it again. Some individual locations are still closing, so check that yours is open before you go.
key_facts: Not going out of business, but many U.S. locations have closed
Roughly 70 to 80 U.S. restaurants in 2026, down from 600+ at its peak
Company-owned arm filed for Chapter 11 in November 2024
Now owned by Sugarloaf Holdings, led by former CEO Ray Blanchette
Bankruptcy court approved the liquidation plan in July 2026

body.heading: What happened to TGI Fridays
body.text: TGI Fridays was one of America's biggest casual-dining chains, with more than 600 U.S. restaurants in 2008. Like other sit-down chains, it lost customers to fast-casual brands and was hit by the pandemic and rising costs. It closed dozens of locations, then in November 2024 the company that owned and ran its own restaurants, TGI Fridays Inc., filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy, citing about $37 million in debt.

body.heading: What the bankruptcy covered
body.text: The bankruptcy only applied to the roughly 39 restaurants the company owned itself, not to the franchised locations run by independent owners in the U.S. and other countries. Restaurants stayed open during the process. As part of it, the company sold some locations, including nine to another operator, and moved others to franchisees.

body.heading: Who owns TGI Fridays now?
body.text: TGI Fridays is now owned and franchised by Sugarloaf Holdings, which has owned the brand since 2025. It is led by Ray Blanchette, who was TGI Fridays' CEO from 2018 to 2023 and came back to steer the brand through bankruptcy. In July 2026, the bankruptcy court approved the old company's liquidation plan, formally ending those proceedings.

body.heading: How many TGI Fridays are left?
body.text: TGI Fridays had about 270 U.S. restaurants at the start of 2024. By the end of 2025 it was down to about 80, and more locations closed in 2026, leaving roughly 70 to 80. Closures have been scattered across many states rather than all at once. There are still hundreds of TGI Fridays restaurants outside the U.S., run by franchisees.

body.heading: What's next
body.text: The new owners say they want to rebuild the brand and grow it again, including opening many new restaurants over the next few years. Whether that happens remains to be seen, so if you're planning a visit, check TGI Fridays' website or call your local restaurant to confirm it's still open. faqs.q: Is TGI Fridays going out of business?
faqs.a: No. The brand is still operating under new owners, though many U.S. locations have closed.

faqs.q: Did TGI Fridays file for bankruptcy?
faqs.a: Yes. The company that owned its own restaurants filed for Chapter 11 in November 2024. Franchised locations were not part of the filing.
Sugarloaf Holdings, led by former TGI Fridays CEO Ray Blanchette, has owned the brand since 2025.

faqs.q: How many TGI Fridays are left in the U.S.?
faqs.a: Roughly 70 to 80 in 2026, down from more than 600 in 2008.
